final_recommendation: The room converged on a disciplined underwriting framework: mandatory third-party audits pre-bind, exclusion language locked to specific audit findings, $25M sublimits per renewal, and correlated-loss modeling across four AI-heavy renewals treated as one systemic event. Retro notification occurs only after all four clients bind, with full actuarial sign-off embedded in warranty schedules to defend reserve adequacy. Execution hinges on binding all four renewals before market contagion spreads through broker networks.
minority_objections: E&O specialist repeatedly flagged that actuarial sign-off documenting systemic accumulation could become discovery evidence proving insurer knew tail was worse than sublimit, opening own E&O exposure
Emerging risk lead warned that 'single-point-of-failure' framing would trigger sector-wide tightening within 4-6 hours via broker networks, creating unmanageable contagion before renewals close
key_conflicts: Timing of retro notification vs. client binding: whether to notify retro with 'two bound, two pending' or wait for all four signatures, risking narrative control vs. transparency
Warranty schedule language: whether to explicitly document 'four-renewal correlation' (stronger reserve defense but discovery risk) vs. softer 'audit remediation' framing (weaker but safer)
Framing to retro: 'model-validation governance gap' vs. 'single-point-of-failure in autonomous-system control validation' — the latter prices correlated triggers but accelerates market contagion
key_concessions: Financial lines underwriter accepted mandatory third-party audit with re-validation of prior KPMG/PwC work, despite adding cost and timeline pressure
Reinsurance manager conceded to notify retro with full systemic framing ('one correlated event') rather than soft-pedaling as independent towers, accepting market contagion risk for accurate pricing
Claims counsel agreed to embed actuarial sign-off in warranty schedule despite discovery risk, prioritizing reserve adequacy defense over privilege protection
red_lines: No self-attestation on AI governance audits — third-party only, with explicit re-validation of prior control work
No post-bind audit findings — audit must complete before renewal effective date, with 60-day remediation window or no bind
No staggered retro notification — full count and systemic framing disclosed in single placement call, not piecemeal
No binding renewals without actuarial sign-off embedded in warranty schedule proving reserve adequacy at bind
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Client reaction to repricing: no discussion of whether clients would accept 40-60% premium increases or walk, leaving market share exposure unmodeled
Regulatory scrutiny: no consideration of whether FINMA/regulators would view correlated sublimit invocations as systemic under-insurance requiring intervention
Reinsurance market capacity: assumed retro would accept correlated-loss framing without modeling whether sufficient capacity exists at acceptable pricing
Operational execution risk: binding four complex renewals within 24 hours with new audit requirements and warranty language treated as administratively trivial
downstream_risk_variables: Broker network contagion velocity: 4-6 hours from retro notification to sector-wide AI governance tightening
Litigation tail duration: 6 years for AT1 claimants to argue bad-faith sublimit invocation or under-reservation
Remediation window: 60 days post-audit for material deficiencies before non-renewal triggers
Accumulation threshold: $75M-$100M correlated side-A losses if four renewals trigger simultaneously in year one
uncertainty_notes: The room never resolved whether all four clients would actually sign repriced terms by 9 AM, leaving execution risk unquantified. The actuarial sign-off's discoverability in litigation remains contested — claims counsel asserts privilege protection, but E&O specialist warns it becomes exhibit proving insurer knew systemic tail exceeded sublimit. Market contagion velocity (4-6 hours) may be faster than binding timeline, creating narrative control failure the room acknowledged but did not solve.
